angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 967,023 km at 128.52 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.7811 +/- 0.0118 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 128.52 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.39 +/- 0.09 solar radii from Ment et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-2 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..213M/abstract): 967,023 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.33 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Ment et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-2 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..213M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6380 K from Ment et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-2 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..213M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Ment et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-2 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..213M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-2.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.276, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
